node.label: Convert mixed number to improper
node.description: Rename a mixed number as an equivalent improper fraction.

node.label: Mixed numbers on number line
node.description: Locate mixed numbers and improper fractions on a number line beyond one whole.

node.label: Compare mixed and improper fractions

node.subject: Mathematics

node.label: Divide fraction by whole number

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reciprocal division models

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Fractions can exceed one
node.description: A fraction can represent more than one whole when the counted fractional units exceed one whole.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mixed number has whole and fraction parts
node.description: A mixed number combines a whole-number part and a proper-fraction part as one quantity.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Improper numerator at least denominator
node.description: An improper fraction has a numerator equal to or greater than its denominator.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mixed and improper forms can be equivalent
node.description: A mixed number and an improper fraction can name the same quantity.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Same denominator means common units
node.description: Fractions with the same denominator count the same-sized fractional units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Common denominator creates same unit
node.description: A common denominator renames fractions so they use the same fractional unit size.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Add and subtract fraction units
node.description: Fraction addition and subtraction combine or compare counts of equal fractional units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Multiplying fraction by whole repeats units
node.description: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number repeats the fractional quantity that many times.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Fraction times fraction means part of part
node.description: Multiplying two fractions can represent taking a fractional part of a fractional part.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Division splits fractional quantity
node.description: Dividing a fraction can mean sharing a fractional quantity or asking how many fractional groups fit.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Improper fractions are invalid
node.description: Learner treats fractions greater than one as wrong because the numerator is not smaller than the denominator.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mixed number parts are unrelated
node.description: Learner treats the whole-number and fractional parts of a mixed number as separate unrelated numbers.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Add denominators when adding fractions
node.description: Learner adds denominators as well as numerators when adding fractions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Common denominator changes value
node.description: Learner thinks renaming to a common denominator changes the quantity rather than the notation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Fraction multiplication always increases
node.description: Learner assumes multiplication with fractions must make a quantity larger.

edge.rationale: Mixed and improper fraction work directly practises quantities greater than one whole.
Mixed-number notation is central to the broad topic.
Improper-fraction notation is central to the broad topic.
Converting improper fractions to mixed numbers directly practises equivalent representations beyond one.
Converting mixed numbers to improper fractions directly practises equivalent representations beyond one.
Number lines help represent mixed and improper quantities beyond one whole.
Comparing forms practises recognising equivalent or ordered mixed and improper quantities.
Adding same-denominator fractions is an early core fraction operation.
Subtracting same-denominator fractions is an early core fraction operation.
Common denominators are central to many fraction operations.
Adding unlike-denominator fractions is a core operation requiring equivalence.
Subtracting unlike-denominator fractions is a core operation requiring equivalence.
Multiplying fractions by whole numbers is a common bridge from whole-number multiplication to fraction multiplication.
Fraction-by-fraction multiplication is a core fraction operation.
Dividing fractional quantities by whole numbers extends sharing and scaling with fractions.
Reciprocal division models support later formal fraction-division procedures.
Understanding fractions greater than one builds on locating non-unit fractional quantities on number lines.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats every fraction as less than one regardless of the numerator.

edge.rationale: Mixed numbers represent quantities greater than one as whole numbers plus fractional parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads the whole-number and fractional parts as two unrelated quantities.

edge.rationale: Improper fraction notation represents quantities at or above one whole by counting fractional units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner rejects 7/4 because the numerator is greater than the denominator.

edge.rationale: Converting improper fractions to mixed numbers requires interpreting the improper fraction as counted fractional units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify how many wholes are contained in the numerator count.

edge.rationale: Converting mixed numbers to improper fractions requires interpreting the whole-number and fractional parts as one quantity.
edge.failure_signal: Learner appends numbers or changes notation without preserving value.

edge.rationale: Locating mixed numbers on a number line requires interpreting the notation as a quantity beyond one whole.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places 2 1/3 at 1/3 or at 21/3 rather than between 2 and 3.

edge.rationale: Comparing mixed and improper forms often requires converting or interpreting equivalent quantities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares surface notation rather than represented magnitude.

edge.rationale: Adding same-denominator fractions requires counting equal-sized fractional units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds denominators instead of combining counts of the same unit.

edge.rationale: Subtracting same-denominator fractions uses the same common-unit structure as addition.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot explain subtraction as removing a count of same-sized fractional units.

edge.rationale: Creating common denominators depends on generating equivalent fractions without changing value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes denominators without scaling numerators consistently.

edge.rationale: Adding unlike-denominator fractions requires first creating common fractional units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds unlike units directly or adds denominators.

edge.rationale: Subtracting unlike-denominator fractions requires first creating common fractional units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner subtracts unlike units directly or subtracts denominators.

edge.rationale: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number can be interpreted as repeated addition of equal fractional quantities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect 3 × 2/5 with three groups of two fifths.

edge.rationale: Fraction-by-fraction multiplication extends multiplication from repeated fractional quantities to parts of parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies whole-number multiplication expectations and assumes the product must be larger.

edge.rationale: Dividing a fraction by a whole number extends equal sharing to fractional quantities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot model splitting a fraction into equal parts.

edge.rationale: Reciprocal models build from simpler fraction division situations but require additional later formalisation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner memorises invert-and-multiply without interpreting the quantities.
